title: 悬垂的白爪 / The Hanging Paw
input_provenance: AI-generated fictional pet photograph; no real person's pet is depicted.
workflow: Generate fictional photographic input, inspect it, then edit that exact image into a graphite-imprint artwork.

before.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create one original editorial pet photograph as the input image for a later art transformation demonstration. This is a fictional cat, not any real person's pet. Portrait 4:5 composition. A relaxed adult black-and-white tuxedo cat lounges over the rounded arm of a beautiful old mustard-ochre velvet armchair. One white front paw dangles comfortably over the front of the arm; the other is folded under its chest. The cat's head is slightly cocked and looking directly at the camera with calm vivid green eyes. Distinctive identity: a black cap covering the ears and upper face, a narrow asymmetrical white blaze between the eyes, a clearly visible small black crescent spot beside one side of the pink nose, white muzzle and bib, white front paws; the black coat ends in a natural uneven boundary across the cheek. Preserve believable feline proportions and clear limb anatomy. Both ears fully inside frame.

Beautiful but unposed everyday presence, slightly mischievous and soft. Late-afternoon window light from the side illuminates individual guard hairs and fine whiskers, natural textured fur and velvet nap. The mustard chair has a little elegant wear, no tears or dirty stains. A muted warm olive wall behind, no clutter, plants, lettering or added props. The cat and its dangling white paw form a readable diagonal across the middle, with the curved chair arm balancing it. Fine photographic detail, quiet color relationship between black, ivory, ochre and green. Shallow but sufficient depth of field: eyes and nose sharp, chair edges gently soft, natural optical falloff. No cartoon effect, no artificial shiny eyes, no oversaturated HDR, no human-like grin, no extra paws, no collar, no text, watermark, border, frame or collage. The entire output is one convincing photographic scene.

after.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve and style-transfer. Edit the attached fictional-cat photograph into a finished 'Soul Imprint / 灵魂拓印' artwork, selective tactile graphite impressions on fresh white paper. The input is the exact subject and composition authority. Preserve the SAME cat, distinctive asymmetrical white blaze, ear shapes and angles, the black spot to the viewer's right of its nose, its calm forward gaze, head tilt, muzzle proportions and natural limb anatomy. Preserve the relaxed pose: one long white foreleg hangs down the front of the armchair at lower center-left, the other white paw rests folded on top of the arm at center-right. Maintain the original framing, relative scale and portrait 4:5 composition. Do not turn this into a new cat, alter the expression, curl it into a ball, or remove a paw.

Transform the photographic scene into a selective dry graphite transfer, with missing information as an essential part of the image. Use a few confident dark charcoal-grey fragments within the forehead cap, near the upper eyelids, the exact nose-side black spot, and a short portion of the dark shoulder. These dark marks have broken, physically deposited edges, irregular fine grain and small untouched gaps, like an incomplete transfer lifted from a sheet. Break up the larger black fur areas into distinct contact-like islands and silvery wisps following the fur's growth. Make some sections of the shoulder, flank, lower foreleg and ear perimeter genuinely disappear into unmarked paper. Do not merely lower the contrast of a normal pencil drawing or spread a uniform distressed texture across it.

The white blaze, muzzle, chest and hanging white paw become luminous unmarked paper with only essential gentle edge traces. Keep the living tenderness of the face legible through restrained eye/eyelid, nose and muzzle marks; no black vacant sockets, no mechanical cross-hatching, no drawn individual hairs everywhere. The eyes become subtle graphite tones, no green color remains. The black nose spot remains a readable identifying accent. Several whiskers can survive as fragile broken strokes; others vanish naturally.

Retain only enough of the armchair's rounded arm and two upholstery seam segments to explain the cat's support and the dangling paw. The mustard color and dense upholstery texture disappear into the page. A curved sparse graphite trace underneath the resting paw and a faint vertical seam below it are sufficient. All background wall and peripheral chair information fades into quiet clean white. The cat's face is the visual focus; a secondary small dark shoulder mark and the suspended white paw create a graceful rhythm. Several larger sections of the image should be completely untouched paper, alongside areas of medium and strong imprint, so it remains visually arresting at thumbnail size while intimate up close.

Entire image is a flat art reproduction on bright neutral-to-slightly-cool white kozo-like paper. Extremely subtle fine fibers, no yellowing, no dirty stains, no background grey wash, no full-page paper-wrinkle filter. One or two faint handling creases may occur far from the face. No literal contact with an animal, no wrapped or pressed anatomy, no taxidermy, sadness or ghost effects. The subject stays alive and relaxed. No frame, labels, writing, signature, mat, tabletop, hands, extra objects, or before/after collage. No photoreal fur or living cat placed on top of paper. The visual language is a luminous, fragmented graphite impression, with precise identity carried by a few surviving marks.

quality_notes: The same head angle, asymmetrical white blaze, nose-side black spot, resting paw and hanging white foreleg are retained. Chair geometry remains as a few sparse supporting curves; broad black fur becomes broken deposited patches. No additional revision used.
